results.problem: QAOA expectation value evaluation for MaxCut (Eval_p^MC)
results.previous_best: NP-hard for every fixed p \ge 2 (Wang et al. [5])
results.quote: For unweighted simple graphs, \(\text{Eval}_1^\text{MC}\in\mathsf{FP}\), \(\text{Eval}_p^\text{MC}\text{\textit{is}}\#P\text{\textit{-hard for every fixed}}p\ge 2\).

results.problem: Single two-qubit correlator evaluation \langle Z_r Z_s \rangle for QAOA MaxCut
results.bound: \#P\text{-hard for every fixed } p \ge 2 \text{ (same hardness as the global expectation)}
results.previous_best: NP-hardness for global expectation (Ref. [5]); correlator hardness not previously established
results.quote: The same conclusions of the theorem hold if the oracle evaluates only one designated two-qubit correlator \(\langle Z_rZ_s\rangle\) rather than the global cost expectation value \(\langle C_G\rangle\).

results.problem: QAOA expectation value evaluation for MaxCut on diameter-two graphs
results.bound: \#P\text{-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions even on connected, unweighted, simple graphs of diameter two}
results.previous_best: \#P-hard on general graphs (Theorem 1.2); no prior diameter-two restriction
results.quote: For every fixed \(p\ge 2\), exact evaluation of the MaxCut QAOA expectation is \(\#P\)-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions, even when restricted to connected, unweighted, simple graphs of diameter two.

results.problem: Exponentially precise additive evaluation of QAOA MaxCut expectation
results.bound: \#P\text{-hard for additive error } \le 2^{-\alpha N} \text{ for some constant } \alpha > 0
results.previous_best: Exact evaluation \#P-hard (Theorem 1.2); no prior exponentially precise approximation hardness
results.quote: Fix \(p\ge 2\) and the mixer angle choices of Theorem 1.2. There exists a constant \(\alpha>0\) such that the following problem is \(\#P\)-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions: given an \(N\)-vertex MaxCut instance from the family constructed in the proof and a tied phase angle specified by the exact algebraic input \(z=e^{\mathrm{i}\phi}\), return a rational number \(\widetilde{F}_G(\phi)\) satisfying \(\left|\widetilde{F}_G(\phi)-F_G(\phi)\right|\le 2^{-\alpha N}\).

results.problem: Phase derivatives of QAOA MaxCut expectation F_G^{(r)}(\phi)
results.bound: \#P\text{-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions for every fixed } p \ge 2 \text{ and } r \ge 1
results.previous_best: No earlier \#P-hardness result for exact derivatives of the standard fixed-depth QAOA for MaxCut objective
results.quote: For every fixed \(p\ge 2\) and every fixed integer \(r\ge 1\), exact computation of \(F_G^{(r)}(\phi)=\frac{dr}{d\phi^r}F_G(\phi)\) is \(\#P\)-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions.

results.problem: Full gradient and Hessian of QAOA MaxCut objective
results.quote: Exact computation of the full gradient \(\nabla\mathcal{F}_G\) and of the full Hessian \(\nabla^2\mathcal{F}_G\) is \(\#P\)-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions.

results.problem: Exponentially precise approximation of QAOA phase derivatives
results.bound: \#P\text{-hard for additive error at most } 2^{-cN} \text{ for some constant } c > 0
results.previous_best: Exact derivative computation \#P-hard (Theorem 3.1); no prior exponentially precise derivative approximation hardness
results.quote: For the mixer angles of Theorem 1.2 and every fixed \(r\ge 1\), there exists a constant \(c>0\) such that approximating \(F_G^{(r)}(\phi)\) to additive error at most \(2^{-cN}\), where \(N=|V(G)|\), is \(\#P\)-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions.

results.problem: Single-query exact QAOA MaxCut expectation evaluation
results.bound: \#P\text{-hard under a deterministic polynomial-time reduction making one oracle call}
results.previous_best: Polynomially many queries (Theorem 1.2); single-query hardness not previously established
results.quote: Under the explicit number field representation above, for every fixed \(p\ge 2\), exact evaluation of the MaxCut QAOA expectation is \(\#P\)-hard under a deterministic polynomial-time reduction making one oracle call.
